passages.t: ‘When I choose a time, I will judge fairly’
passages.happening:
The heading reads, “For the choirmaster: To the tune of ‘Do Not Destroy.’ A Psalm of Asaph. A song” (verse 1). The people begin with thanks. “We give thanks to You, O God; we give thanks, for Your Name is near” (verse 1).

Then God himself speaks. “When I choose a time, I will judge fairly” (verse 2). When the earth shakes, he is the one who holds up its pillars (verse 3). He warns the proud not to boast, and not to lift up their horn (verses 4 to 5).

The singer explains. Honour does not come from the east or the west or the desert, “but it is God who judges; He brings down one and exalts another” (verse 7). In the LORD's hand is a cup of strong wine, and the wicked must drink it to the dregs (verse 8).

The singer promises to keep praising (verse 9). God has the last word: “All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be exalted” (verse 10).
passages.hearers:
Psalm 75 comes straight after Psalm 74, which ended with no answer. Here God speaks. Whoever arranged the Psalms may have meant this: the cry of the ruined temple, and then God's reply that he has not lost control. He will judge, at the time he chooses.

‘Do Not Destroy’ was probably the name of a tune. The same words head Psalms 57, 58 and 59.

The horn was a picture of strength, taken from a wild ox or a ram tossing its head. To ‘lift up your horn’ was to strut and defy. To have your horn ‘exalted’ was to be given honour. Hannah used the same picture when she sang after Samuel was born (1 Samuel 2:1).

The cup in verse 8 was a picture the prophets used often. A host passed a cup to guests. But this cup is God's judgment, and those who drink it stagger. ‘The dregs’ are the thick, bitter bits at the bottom.
passages.later:
Hannah sang, “The LORD sends poverty and wealth; He humbles and He exalts” (1 Samuel 2:7). Mary sang the same truth when she carried Jesus: “He has brought down rulers from their thrones, but has exalted the humble” (Luke 1:52).

In the garden of Gethsemane, Jesus prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me” (Matthew 26:39). Christians have long read that cup as the cup of judgment the prophets spoke of, which Jesus drank for others.
passages.asks:
Where are you trying to lift your own horn? Psalm 75 says that honour does not come from the right connections or the right direction. It comes from God.

If you are waiting for wrongs to be put right, hear verse 2. God chooses the time. That can be hard to wait for. But it means that the waiting is not wasted, and that the last word is his.
